stories.headline: Nvidia unveils RTX Spark Arm PC chip with MediaTek; Microsoft uses it in Surface Laptop Ultra

key_facts.fact: Nvidia announced the RTX Spark, an Arm-based consumer PC chip family co-developed with MediaTek, pitched as 'the most efficient PC chip ever built'.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia announces the RTX Spark, an Arm-based consumer PC chip family that it says is 'the most efficient PC chip ever built', made in partnership with MediaTek. Nvidia enters the consumer laptop realm.

key_facts.fact: RTX Spark offers up to 20 CPU cores and a Blackwell GPU with 6,144 CUDA cores, with up to 128GB of unified memory, capable of '100 FPS 1440p gaming' or running 120B-parameter models locally.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia says RTX Spark offers up to 20 CPU cores and a Blackwell GPU with 6,144 CUDA cores, capable of '100 FPS 1440p gaming' or running 120B-parameter models

key_facts.fact: Microsoft unveiled the Surface Laptop Ultra powered by RTX Spark, with a 15-inch mini-LED touchscreen and up to 128GB of unified memory, shipping fall 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft unveils the Surface Laptop Ultra, with an Nvidia RTX Spark SoC, a 15" mini-LED touchscreen, and up to 128GB of unified memory, coming this fall

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang said Microsoft and Nvidia will 'reinvent the PC', starting with 30+ laptops and 10 desktops in the fall from Dell, HP, Lenovo, Acer, Asus, Gigabyte and MSI.
key_facts.excerpt: Jensen Huang says Microsoft and Nvidia will 'reinvent the PC', starting with 30+ laptops and 10 desktops coming in the fall from Dell, HP, Lenovo, and others

stories.headline: Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform enters full production; Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceX among first Vera CPU users

key_facts.fact: Nvidia said its Vera Rubin computing platform is ramping into 'full production', with first systems expected to ship in the fall after a March announcement.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia says its Vera Rubin computing platform is ramping into 'full production', with first systems expected to ship in the fall, after a March announcement

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang said Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX are among the first big users of Nvidia's upcoming Vera CPUs, which it says are 1.8x faster for AI workloads than x86 chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia Corp. said Anthropic PBC, OpenAI and SpaceX are among the first big users of its upcoming microprocessor. Vera CPUs are 1.8x faster for AI workloads than x86 chips.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia also unveiled DGX Station, a desktop Windows PC powered by its GB300 Grace Blackwell chip with up to 768 GB of memory, capable of running 1 trillion-parameter models locally, starting at about $92,000.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia unveils DGX Station, a desktop Windows PC powered by its GB300 Grace Blackwell chip with up to 748 GB of memory, capable of running 1T-parameter models. The desktop is DGX Station with GB300! It does have 768GB of memory. It also starts at ~$92,000

stories.headline: Intel details Crescent Island data center GPUs with up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X, skipping HBM for inference

key_facts.fact: Intel detailed its Crescent Island data center GPUs at Computex 2026, based on its Xe3P architecture and 'built for agentic AI'.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel details its Crescent Island data center GPUs based on its Xe3P architecture and using LPDDR5X memory instead of HBM, calling them 'built for agentic AI'

key_facts.fact: The Crescent Island GPUs use LPDDR5X memory instead of HBM, with up to 480 GB per accelerator, an unusual choice intended to combat HBM shortages and bring more AI data closer to the chip.
key_facts.excerpt: Boasts up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X to combat memory shortages. Unusual memory choice brings lots of AI data closer to the chip for efficiency.

sources.title: Intel details long-awaited Crescent Island AI GPU at Computex

stories.headline: Intel launches Xeon 6+ Clearwater Forest CPUs on 18A; claims 30% single-thread lead over AMD Epyc 9965

key_facts.fact: Intel unveiled six Xeon 6+ data center CPU SKUs codenamed Clearwater Forest, marking the first deployment of Intel's 18A process in the data center, with up to 288 cores and 576 MB of L3 cache.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel Xeon 6+ Clearwater Forest puts 18A in the data center with up to 288 cores, 576 MB of L3 cache. Intel's dense Xeon 6+ design marks the first time 18A is being deployed in the data center.

key_facts.fact: Intel said its new Xeon 6990E+ delivers 30% better single-thread performance and up to 30% more energy efficiency than AMD's 192-core Epyc 9965.
key_facts.excerpt: New Xeon 6990E+ is 30 percent faster per thread than 192-core AMD Epyc 9965, says Intel

key_facts.fact: Intel also teased its next-generation Xeon 7 Diamond Rapids on the Intel 18A-P node with PCIe 6.0, 50% more cores and twice the memory bandwidth versus Xeon 6, launching in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel Xeon 7 Diamond Rapids CPUs officially launching in 2027 on Intel 18A-P. Next-gen P-core Xeon features PCIe 6.0, 50 percent higher core counts and twice the memory bandwidth.

stories.headline: Nvidia unveils open humanoid reference Isaac GR00T and Cosmos 3 physical AI foundation model

key_facts.fact: Nvidia unveiled Isaac GR00T, an open humanoid reference design powered by its Jetson Thor chip, combining a Unitree H2 Plus robot body with Sharpa five-fingered hands.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia unveils Isaac GR00T, an open humanoid reference design powered by its Jetson Thor chip, combining a Unitree H2 Plus robot and Sharpa five-fingered hands

key_facts.fact: Nvidia said it plans to work with humanoid robot makers in the U.S., Europe and South Korea, in addition to China's Unitree.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia plans to work with humanoid robot makers in the U.S., Europe and South Korea in addition to China's Unitree

key_facts.fact: Nvidia also unveiled Cosmos 3, an open physical AI foundation model to help robots and autonomous cars better understand the real world with limited training data.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia unveils Cosmos 3, an open physical AI foundation model, to help robots and autonomous cars better understand the real world with limited training data

stories.headline: China toughens outbound investment rules, expanding scrutiny of overseas tech and data deals

key_facts.fact: China issued new investment rules expanding regulator powers to scrutinize overseas deals involving Chinese investors, technology, and data, effective from July 1, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: China issues new investment rules, expanding regulator powers to scrutinize overseas deals involving Chinese investors, tech, and data, effective from July 1

key_facts.fact: The rules follow controversy over Meta's reported moves around Chinese AI startup Manus, which became a flashpoint over outbound technology flows.
key_facts.excerpt: China toughens rules on outbound investment after Meta-Manus contention

key_facts.fact: A 'tier-one' chipmaker participated in the round, which Invisix says will fund work to transform chip metrology.
